seoTitle: Change Language in GoDaddy Website, Emails & Domains
metaDescription: Switch your GoDaddy dashboard, website, emails, and domain settings to English or another language for easier account and billing management.
intro: GoDaddy sometimes defaults new accounts to a language based on your location or the browser you signed up with, which can make the dashboard feel unfamiliar even though nothing about your domain or hosting has actually changed. This guide walks through the real path into your account — the sign-in screen and the My Account dashboard you land on — and where the language preference lives from there, so you can switch the interface to English or another supported language without second-guessing whether you're in the right menu.

steps.heading: Sign in to your GoDaddy account
steps.body: Go to godaddy.com and sign in with your username or customer number and password. You can also sign in with Apple, Facebook, or Google if your account is linked that way, and there's a "Keep me signed in on this device" checkbox worth using if this is your own computer, since language and other display preferences are tied to the account you're logged into, not the browser.

image.caption: The GoDaddy sign-in screen, where you authenticate before reaching account and language settings.

steps.heading: Land on the My Account dashboard
steps.body: After signing in you arrive at My Account, GoDaddy's central hub for domains, hosting, email, and billing. This is also where account-wide settings live, accessed through the avatar or account-name dropdown in the top-right corner next to the help icon and notification bell. Any banners about SMS alerts or payment methods you see here are unrelated to language — dismiss them and head for that account menu instead.

image.caption: The My Account dashboard after sign-in, with the account menu in the top-right corner where profile and preference settings are reached.

steps.heading: Open your profile and preference settings
steps.body: From the account dropdown, open your profile or account settings area. This is where GoDaddy groups personal details like your name, contact information, and — depending on your account type — a language or region preference. If you don't see it immediately under the main profile tab, check for a dedicated "Preferences" or "Communication" section, since GoDaddy has moved this setting between menus across redesigns.

steps.heading: Select your preferred language
steps.body: Choose English, or whichever supported language you want, from the dropdown or list of options. Save the change, and the dashboard should refresh in the new language immediately — if it doesn't apply right away, a full page reload or a fresh sign-in usually clears it up.

steps.heading: Check that emails and domain notices follow along
steps.body: The dashboard language and the language of GoDaddy's automated emails aren't always tied to the same single toggle. After changing your preference, watch the next renewal reminder, security notice, or domain expiration email to confirm it arrives in the language you selected. If it doesn't, the communication language may need to be set separately in the same preferences area.

steps.heading: Verify billing and account details display correctly
steps.body: Head back into Billing under My Account and confirm invoices, payment method labels, and renewal terms now display in your chosen language. This matters most if you're managing the account for a client or team in a different region — you want what they see on an invoice to match what they see in the dashboard, not a mix of both.

faq.question: Will changing my GoDaddy language affect my domain settings?
faq.answer: No, changing the display language only changes how information is presented to you in the dashboard — it doesn't alter DNS records, nameservers, or any other actual domain configuration.

faq.question: Can I switch back to a different language later?
faq.answer: Yes, the language preference can be changed again at any time from the same profile or preferences menu in My Account.

faq.question: Does this change affect emails sent to my customers?
faq.answer: No, this setting controls your own account and dashboard language. It doesn't change the language of any store, site, or emails you send to your own customers.

faq.question: Why would my account default to a different language?
faq.answer: GoDaddy often sets an initial language based on your location or browser settings at signup, which is why it can show a language you didn't explicitly choose.

faq.question: I can't find the language setting — where else should I look?
faq.answer: Check the account dropdown in the top-right of My Account first, then look for Profile, Preferences, or Communication settings — GoDaddy has relocated this option across different dashboard redesigns.
